passages.title: The Resettlement of Jerusalem.
passages.text: The Chronicler focuses on the worship personnel who return to Jerusalem from exile.

passages.title: 1 Chron 9:3–9
passages.text: Repopulated Jerusalem includes people from **Ephraim** and **Manasseh**, as well as **Judah** and **Benjamin**. The Judahites are listed as descendants of the patriarch’s sons.

passages.title: 1 Chron 9:10–13
passages.text: The **priests** in postexilic Jerusalem are praised for their temple ministry. Their numbers (**1,760**) have grown significantly (compare 1,192 in Neh. 11:12–14 ).

passages.title: 1 Chron 9:14–16
passages.text: Levitical singers and musicians include descendants of **Asaph** and **Jeduthun**, choir leaders in David’s day ( 6:39 ; 25:1 ).

passages.title: 1 Chron 9:17–32
passages.text: The Levitical gatekeepers’ authority is traced to their service under **Phinehas** (v. 20 ; see Num. 25:6–11 ) and their appointment by **David** ( 1 Chron. 9:22 ; 26:1–32 ). Along with their primary duty of safeguarding the temple, the gatekeepers were also responsible for the **utensils** and supplies used in the daily sacrifices ( 9:28–32 ).

passages.title: The Genealogy of Saul.
passages.text: This is repeated from 8:29–38 to introduce the Chronicler’s account of Saul’s reign (ch. 10 ). While Saul’s dynasty ended with his death ( 10:6 ), his family line continued for many generations ( 9:40–44 ).
